I see where you are coming from, but I think the situation is complex. Let me toss out an over-sized example, and then talk about the smaller content like "Cool fireworks pic":

Let's say this fall, humans unexpectedly land a person on Mars (maybe China was secretly working on it). Reddit's front page will be filled with info about it. Should we avoid mentioning it here, because we'd be "copying them?" Should we mention the landing, but not mention any insights that are being discussed at Reddit? If it suddenly happens this summer, they're going to get Buzz Aldrin in an AMA - that's just a fact. But of course, that item will be in all the news everywhere, and not just on [other site].

I recognize that a sudden Mars mission would be a "big ticket item" of news. But if something simple like "Cool fireworks pic" is getting thousands of upvotes at [other site], it seems this (Voat) community would like it, too. It seems we can approach these smaller but popular items in one of two ways:

1) Discourage cross-posting it here.

But there is an unintended consequence: Many people will never fully leave [other site] because there is stuff over there that you can't get at Voat. If we self-censor things just because they are popular on Reddit, I think many people will keep their Reddit accounts active so they can easily go browse the "hot info" they'd otherwise miss out on.

or

2) Cross-post some of it here.

But there are two unintended consequences. First, as you say, we'll look like a bunch of "me too!'s. Second, if the content from Reddit is just their "top couple of dozen" links, those links will be inherently potent and will have a drowning out effect that might limit the effectiveness of producing OC on Voat. In other words, the "superstar" articles from Reddit will get 1,000 upVoats, while locally generated Voat OC stuff might only get a few hundred upVoats.

I recognize that this is a devilishly hard choice, but it is the choice before us, and I suspect we'll never all be "as one" on the issue, since the trade offs are rather great no matter which way you go with it ("1)" or "2)" above).

I think maybe taking the very top things posted to [other site] and pollenating them over here is not such a bad idea, because much of Voat's population is ex-Reddit (even the people who've been at Voat for a year). Therefore, highly-rnanked conten from [other site] will almost surely be of interest to Voaters if it is stirring a lot of interest at [other site]. But like you, I do want Voat to be it's own kickass site by its own right.

tl;dr: I'm torn.
